To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) we develop an entity-graph based approach for reasoning with general knowledge, and (ii) this leads to a significant improvement in accuracy for FVQA.
1) a graph convolutional neural network (GCN) is an effective model for FVQA, and 2) the GCN is trained end-to-end with an attention mechanism to focus on important entities.
(1) a graph convolutional net is a better choice than a deep net for the FVQA task; and (2) reasoning with a graph of entities is a more effective approach than considering one fact at a given time.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: How can we reason with facts to answer visual questions?
the following three questions: How do we reason with a large set (hundreds) of facts to answer a given question? Can a graph convolutional net help? How can we improve on the FVQA task?
developing a novel reasoning approach for FVQA that outperforms the state of the arts by a large margin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method outperforms all previous methods on the FVQA task by a large margin.
the proposed approach, which jointly reasons about all entities, outperforms the state of the-art on the challenging FvQA dataset by 7%.
we have proposed a novel graph based approach to FVQA, which outperforms state of the art methods.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are proposing a novel approach to answer questions about a given image by reasoning about the facts.
we are able to reason over the graph structure of entities to answer questions.
we propose to use the fact-based visual question answering task to study the ability of deep networks to perform reasoning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
reasoning with general knowledge is a global rather than local problem and that a graph convolutional net provides a suitable architecture to address this challenge.
reasoning with facts can be achieved by using a graph convolutional net.
reasoning about a question-image pair requires considering the entire graph of entities and their relations rather than considering them one-by-one.
